report.headline: Usage projected to rise to 25.3% in the EuroLeague, but the accompanying efficiency projection fails its own reliability check

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 25.3% in the EuroLeague, up from a 20.1% usage rate in the 2008-09 NBA season, placing the subject above the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average of 20.5%.

risks.text: The true shooting projection of 58.6% should not be trusted: the model's error on this metric (4.5%) is worse than the trivial league-mean baseline (4.3%), meaning it adds no information beyond guessing the EuroLeague average.

The 95% prediction interval for usage (19.0% to 31.5%) covers more than three EuroLeague standard deviations (sd 4.1%), so while the model can rank this player as likely above average, it cannot price his exact role.

Unlike the typical assumption that players who change leagues are already well above their league's average, the cohort of 115 historical NBA-to-EuroLeague movers this estimate rests on actually sat 0.31 standard deviations below their own league's average, an atypical selection pattern worth flagging.
Even setting aside its unreliability, the fitted true-shooting slope of 0.532 implies only about half of a player's shooting standing relative to his league would be expected to carry over.

strengths.text: Projected usage of 25.3% sits nearly a full league standard deviation above the EuroLeague average of 20.5% (sd 4.1%), suggesting an above-average offensive role even at the low end of the interval.
Source-season true shooting of 55.2% was already 0.17 standard deviations above the NBA average that year, reflecting efficient scoring on his NBA usage.

The usage projection is backed by a model that actually beats the trivial league-mean baseline (3.2% mean absolute error vs 4.2%), so the usage number carries real information rather than just restating the league average.
The fitted slope for usage rate transitions from NBA to EuroLeague is 0.977, indicating that a player's standing relative to his league tends to carry over almost fully on this metric.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 21.2% to 29.3%, and the 95% interval from 19.0% to 31.5% - a span of roughly two league standard deviations (4.1%), wide enough that the model can say this is likely an above-average usage player in the EuroLeague but cannot pin down where in that range he lands.
